summary: Cascade layers are set up in CSS. The HTML is a row of buttons, and each label names the layer that wins for that button.
notes: The third button has an id and a class. Normally the id rule would win.
Compare each label with the rules in the CSS pane to see why it got that color.
type="button" makes buttons that do nothing when clicked, which is all this demo needs.
pitfall: Adding more ids or classes in the HTML to fight a style you cannot override. With layers you can put the styles in the right order instead.
